clue.text: Move the needle over flier for movie

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them about, so the letters of the next piece are rearranged

parts.note: to needle is to stitch with a needle, i.e. sew
a tern is a seabird, a flier

explanation.surface: Someone advances a dial or a gramophone needle to reach the bit about a pilot in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move the needle' reads as a business cliché, but it shuffles the three letters of the needle's verb. 'Over' places that piece before the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a film genre set on the American frontier, so it is one kind of movie.

clue.text: Injuries with teeth missing at the front

indicators.note: something missing at the front has lost its opening letter

parts.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with
prongs are the teeth of a fork

explanation.surface: A dental patient's mouth has been damaged and the front teeth knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: PRONGS loses its P and W takes its place at the front, giving WRONGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongs are injuries in the legal sense: harms or injustices done to a person.

clue.text: I is iodine — it isn't one character, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.words: is iodine — it isn't one character
parts.note: the closing letters of is, iodine, it, isn't, one and character

explanation.surface: A chemistry pedant insists the symbol I stands for iodine and is not a single letter at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I is iodine' looks like chemistry, but the first I is the definition: in a crossword the I speaking is the compiler. Here 'is' is both its link and the source of the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword compilers refer to themselves as 'I' or 'me' in clues, so the first-person pronoun stands for the compiler.

clue.text: Potential cross-makers largely had to accommodate reader of scripture

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house something, so one piece holds the other inside
largely means for the most part, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: had as in had a meal, i.e. eaten
a lector reads the lessons in a church service

explanation.surface: Someone who largely had to put up a visiting church reader is described in grumbling terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' as in had for dinner; 'largely' trims its ending before it houses the church reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters mark their ballot papers with a cross, so the body of people entitled to vote are potential cross-makers.

clue.text: Notable mother-in-law happening to capture bird that is no longer heading north

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading from bottom to top
capturing something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: happening or fashionable is in
the moa was a flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct

explanation.surface: A famous mother-in-law happens to catch a bird that is no longer migrating northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' looks like part of the movement, but it describes the extinct bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi is Ruth's devoted mother-in-law, the Bible's most famous one.

clue.text: What's inside short story books

parts.note: conte is a term for a short story, borrowed from French
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A question about what lies within short story collections.
explanation.definitionFit: The content of a container or a book is the material held inside it.

clue.text: Noisy building site almost has belief going around it

indicators.note: going around something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a credo is a statement of belief

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a scene is a site, as in the scene of the crime

explanation.surface: A loud construction site is almost wrapped in faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy building' looks like a construction site, but building here means growing in volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness in music, a build-up of sound.

clue.text: Home console from the Eighties finally out

parts.note: the NES was the Nintendo Entertainment System, launched in the 1980s

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the last letter of out

explanation.surface: A retro games console from the Eighties is finally being released for the home market.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a bird's dwelling, and loosely any snug place someone lives.

clue.text: Lift up eggs broken by clumsy valet

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
broken by means split open with something pushed into the gap

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: clumsy handling puts things in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel valet clumsily drops a tray of eggs carried up in the lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevator is the American word for a lift, the car that carries people between floors.

clue.text: Perhaps film director on board to engage personnel

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a tiller steers a boat, so it directs things on board
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A film director on a company board hiring staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' wants to be someone in films; it is the steering lever of a boat, which takes HR inside after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a suspense story, so a film is one example; 'Perhaps' signals the example.

clue.text: Fantastic evangelism saving a companion

indicators.note: saving here means except for, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: outreach is the work of spreading the gospel to new people
taken as written
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A fantastic missionary campaign saves a companion's soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' reads as rescuing but means except: remove A and CH from the end of OUTREACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means bizarre or far beyond convention, the sense of fantastic as wildly unusual.

clue.text: React too strongly, regarding ox

parts.note: over in the sense about, as in arguing over money
a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

explanation.surface: Someone overreacts on the subject of an ox.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversteer is to turn the wheel too much, so a vehicle responds more sharply than intended.

clue.text: After work, cite genera being part of a family

indicators.note: after being worked, material has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A biologist, after the day's work, cites genera belonging to one family in taxonomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Genera and family suggest biological classification, but the family is a human one.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-niece is a sibling's granddaughter, one relation within a family tree.

clue.text: You might see well with this light, it's said

definitions.text: You might see well with this

indicators.note: it's said means the word is heard rather than read, so its spelling may differ

parts.note: light as a colour is pale

explanation.surface: An aid to eyesight that works in light conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See well' sounds like having good eyesight, but the well is a water well and you would see a bucket beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket, the vessel lowered into or used at a well to draw water.

clue.text: Nothing Europe has changes what Covent Garden has

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: changes means the following letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Nothing Europe has can match what London's Covent Garden has.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden in London is home to the Royal Opera House, so the venue is what the district has.

clue.text: I abhor spinners and abhor phone somehow ringing Alastair Campbell, primarily

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so one set of letters surrounds the other
somehow suggests an unexplained process, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters are used

parts.note: the initials of the name

explanation.surface: Someone loathes political spin doctors and hates phoning Alastair Campbell, Tony Blair's notorious press chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Alastair Campbell was Blair's spin doctor, so 'spinners' looks political; the spinners are spiders. The shuffled letters wrap round AC after their first two.
explanation.definitionFit: An arachnophobe has a fear of spiders, which spin webs, so would say they abhor spinners.

clue.text: It says what to do having heard European composer

indicators.note: having heard means the words are taken by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: a Czech is a European
Liszt was the Hungarian composer

explanation.surface: Instructions given after listening to a European composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A checklist is a list of items or tasks to be ticked off, telling you what needs doing.

clue.text: Garden tool succeeded with less round

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
someone less round is slimmer, i.e. trimmer

explanation.surface: A garden tool did the job, with the gardener a little less plump afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A strimmer is the British name for a string trimmer or weed-whacker.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is a powered line trimmer for cutting grass edges, a common gardening implement.

clue.text: Individual copies up amount to be paid

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: to ape is to copy
a rate is a charge or amount payable

explanation.surface: An individual's copies push up the amount they must pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate as an adjective means distinct and individual, each existing apart from the others.

clue.text: Those at Greer plays?

indicators.note: plays suggests letters moving freely about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The audience at plays by someone called Greer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: people at Greer's plays are an audience, and the same words rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatregoers are people who attend plays, so those in the audience at a Greer production qualify.

clue.text: Commonly ducking reel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bobbing up and down, with the final g dropped as in casual speech
second meaning: a spool for thread

explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' signals the dropped g of colloquial speech, written as bobbin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobbin is a spool on which thread or yarn is wound, the same thing as a reel.

clue.text: Hide American city's information

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Someone conceals information about a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb; it is an animal's skin. Skinny is slang for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal usage 'the skinny' means the inside story or the relevant facts on something.

clue.text: Hardware's very cheap promotion?

parts.note: 1p, one penny, is very cheap; the digit 1 is read as I
an ad promotes something

explanation.surface: A hardware store's bargain-basement sales promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often read the digit 1 as the letter I, so 1p, a single penny, gives IP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apple tablet computer is a piece of hardware, a physical device as opposed to software.

clue.text: Start to show sauce, cutting up script where artistic ideas are tried

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of show

indicators.note: cutting means removing part, here the word given straight after it

parts.note: ketchup is a tomato sauce
taken as written; these letters are removed
the book of a musical is its script

explanation.surface: Instructions for a comic show where someone is chopping up a script with sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting up' looks like a single shredding instruction, but it means remove UP from the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketchbook is a pad of paper in which an artist makes rough drawings to try out ideas.

clue.text: Support leaving apart from lock

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the named word goes out of the longer one

parts.note: a buttress is a support built against a wall
but means except, apart from

explanation.surface: A support has gone, apart from the lock on the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a fastening; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Sentimental time to leave former post

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a tweet was a post on Twitter, now renamed X
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A soppy moment as someone says it is time to leave a former job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests a job; it is a social media post, called a tweet before Twitter became X.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee describes something excessively sweet, quaint or mawkish, overly sentimental in taste.

clue.text: King and queen perhaps securing a trick for the audience in the interval

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: king and queen are chess pieces, also called men
taken as written

indicators.note: something for the audience is meant to be heard, so the sound counts

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick

explanation.surface: Royals put on a trick for an audience during the interval at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN holds A to make MEAN, then the sound of a trick follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile means in the intervening time, during the period between two events.

clue.text: Pope to stop tracking Abraham's roots

parts.note: in Genesis, Abraham came from Ur of the Chaldees
to ban is to stop

explanation.surface: A pope moves to end research into Abraham's ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roots' suggests family history, but it means the place Abraham came from. Tracking means following, which sets the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban was the name taken by eight popes, including Urban II who preached the First Crusade.

clue.text: Dodgy caterer having other end of apple put up again

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are disordered
having the other end means one terminal letter is exchanged for the opposite one

parts.note: taken as written
the final letter of apple replaces its first letter

explanation.surface: A shady caterer's apple has gone off at one end.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of CATERER is the first letter of apple; swap in the other end of apple to get CETERER, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-erect a structure is to raise or build it once more after it has come down.

clue.text: Police bulletin about drug rejected by detective, briefly

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are turned round
about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a news bulletin
E is ecstasy

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: A police bulletin about a drugs haul turned down by a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sweeney is London slang for the Flying Squad, from rhyming slang Sweeney Todd (Flying Squad).
explanation.definitionFit: The Sweeney is British slang for the Flying Squad, a Metropolitan Police unit, hence police.
